title: Aerosol Dip Tube Design: Depletion & Spray Consistency
author: Global Aerosols Team

hero.alt: Aerosol dip tube design shown in a clear glass demonstration can on its side, with a dip tube running through amber liquid to the can base — Global Aerosols

diagram.alt: Several aerosol dip tubes of different lengths laid out beside a beaker of amber liquid for length comparison — Global Aerosols diagram

infographic.alt: Aerosol valve assemblies with attached dip tubes in a row beside a glass cutaway can showing the liquid level — Global Aerosols infographic

image_generation_notes: 3 final images + 1 rejected hero regeneration (20 credits each, 80 total). The first hero (upright glass can) filled about 60% of the frame height and could not survive the 1200x630 / in-page banner crop without losing either the actuator or the dip-tube end; it was regenerated with the can lying on its side. The OpenArt CLI has no aspect-ratio flag, so 1:1 1K outputs were centre-cropped and resized.
content_notes: Mechanism claims (vapor tap, bore vs spray rate, tube materials, angled cut, stress-cracking grades) come from aerosol and dip-tube patent literature, stated qualitatively with no dimensions. ASTM D3069 is cited as a historical standard per ASTM's own listing; BlogSkill Section H's 'ASTM D5964 (spray rate)' reference was not used because it could not be verified.
